If sentiment is negative in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% in early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is positive and price is trending down, add 0.5–1.5% to forecast in mid horizon (8–15 days) to capture reversal bias.  
If sentiment is neutral and price is near support, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% in late horizon (16–30 days) to avoid overextension.  
If sentiment swings from negative to positive within 5 days, increase forecast by 1.0–2.0% in early horizon to reflect momentum shift.  
If sentiment is consistently positive and price is above 65, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% in late horizon to avoid overbought bias.  
If sentiment is mixed and price is volatile, apply 0.5–1.0% smoothing to forecast in mid horizon to dampen noise.
